evidence.excerpt: Many clinical laboratory studies involve datasets in which the number of measured analytes or derived features approaches or exceeds the number of patient records. In such settings, feature selection outcomes vary substantially across bootstrap samples of the training data, threatening reproducibility. We examined selection stability for five filter and three wrapper methods applied to six datasets with 80 to 340 samples and 30 to 210 features, all drawn from clinical biochemistry and immunology laboratory records. Stability was quantified with the Nogueira–Brown stability index. Mutual information filtering showed the highest stability index across five of six datasets. Wrapper methods based on recursive feature elimination with support vector machines showed strong predictive performance but low stability indices, with mean index values below 0.45. A two-stage procedure—filter pre-selection followed by wrapper refinement—improved both stability and cross-validated AUC in four datasets. Practical guidelines are provided for laboratories operating under sample-size constraints.
